items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: compared to some piano players, your hands are small compared to an Earl Hines or --

ctx.x: I mean things of that sort are a challenge to you, no matter how great you are. And Ben Webster certainly was one of the most influential parts of Duke Ellington's band in the forties. Up to that point Duke's band had been featuring the saxophone more or less of Johnny Hodges. But Ben Webster actually gave Duke a new life, along with a bass player by the name of Jimmy Blanton. Between the two of these guys they brought new life to Duke Ellington's band, which made it able for him to compete musically with the…
course Earl Hines who had always had a very fine rhythmic orchestration of musicians, you see.

So actually this struggle, I have had that struggle and I still have that struggle. This is part of being an artist, and particularly one who's making a living at the field. And in that sense I could say yes, I've had struggles and I'm still having struggles with myself, in trying to play.
